your_book:
Friday was a mixed-to-soft session for Jaleel's book, with the overall unrealized gain sitting at +6.74% but several meaningful intraday drags pulling against that cushion. The heaviest single-day hit came from Broadcom (AVGO), which fell nearly 6% on the session — newsflow flagging that Stanley Druckenmiller dumped AVGO in Q2 is a credibility headwind even for a small weight. Zoetis (ZTS) shed 2.7% and remains in the red overall at −6.3%, despite carrying a STRONG BUY verdict and the portfolio's highest QARP score among its peer set; that divergence between the model's conviction and price action is widening and deserves honest scrutiny. ServiceNow (NOW) and Adobe (ADBE) each dropped roughly 2.4–2.6%, the former purely on rate/multiple sensitivity and the latter still haunted by AI-disruption narrative rather than numbers.

On the positive side, the book's largest position, Rocket Lab (RKLB) at 15.8% weight, was essentially flat (+0.19%) — which is notable given it carries an AVOID verdict and a QARP of just 36.6, the weakest in the book. That concentration in a flagged name remains the structural tension here. Neurocrine Biosciences (NBIX) was the day's bright spot at +1.26%, although it too sits in the red overall (−6.3%). Boston Scientific (BSX) and Uber (UBER) held steady with negligible moves.

What to watch: the tech cluster (NOW, ADBE, AVGO) is under simultaneous pressure from valuation, narrative, and smart-money exits — three separate vectors converging. NVDA's report on August 26 is the next hard catalyst; the WSJ story about Nvidia downsizing its OpenAI data-center commitment is precisely the kind of AI-capex-doubt headline the risk flag warned about. LULU and AZO are both underwater with September and October catalysts ahead. The book is not in distress, but the drift between model verdicts and price reality — particularly in ZTS, LULU, and RKLB — is getting harder to ignore.

attention.headline: Largest position carries AVOID verdict and lowest QARP in the book
attention.note: At 15.8% weight — nearly double the next largest holding — Rocket Lab's AVOID flag and QARP of 36.6 represent a structural mismatch with a capital-preservation mandate that demands an explicit size or exit decision.

attention.headline: −5.94% Friday; Druckenmiller exit adds narrative pressure
attention.note: A high-profile Q2 dump by Druckenmiller is a sentiment overhang on top of an already borderline HOLD-QUAL verdict and the lowest QARP among the tech names; worth monitoring whether the selling is isolated or signals broader institutional rotation out of the stock.

attention.headline: STRONG BUY / highest QARP yet −6.3% overall and falling
attention.note: The widening gap between the model's top conviction and persistent price weakness in Zoetis is a classic thesis-vs.-price divergence — either the model is early, or something structural in animal-health fundamentals is being mispriced; the August 26 NVDA report won't clarify this, so ZTS needs its own independent re-underwrite.

attention.headline: WSJ: Nvidia downsizing OpenAI data-center commitment ahead of Aug 26 earnings
attention.note: The existing export-control risk flag now has a second vector — AI-capex scaling doubt — and the August 26 report is the next hard test of whether the STRONG BUY verdict survives contact with guidance.
